hardware_dossier.transmitter: Sealed titanium capsule housing an 85-watt solid-state synthesizer and mechanical brass fog-bell acoustic transducer, powered since 2689 by a Strontium-90 RTG.
hardware_dossier.feedline_anomaly: Every local morning at TSol dawn, a herd of tall 4-meter wading silt-striders migrates past Mooring N-24 and rubs their carapace plates against the stainless-steel guy-wires, detuning the vertical whip capacitive hat by -165 Hz.

worldbuilding.habitat_and_culture: Kraken North Shallows on Titan-Minor is a mirror-calm expanse of liquid hydrocarbons shrouded in twilight mist. Because Buoy N-24 is an unstaffed autonomous beacon, the only camera in the shallows is bolted directly to the buoy's own upper steel tripod—looking down past its amber Fresnel lamp and taut stainless guy-wire.
worldbuilding.spectrum_gimmick_title: Biological Capacitive-Hat Theremin (-165 Hz Fauna Guy-Wire Rub)
worldbuilding.hauser_commentary: Titan-Minor on 3890 kilohertz. Automated French tide tables at 0348, followed by that unmistakable downward pitch-bend of 165 Hertz—captured on the buoy's own mast-mounted camera as a Silt-Strider walks right up and rubs its neck against the warm stainless-steel guy-wire!
worldbuilding.qsl_postcard_style: Bureau Hydrographique Onboard Mast-Cam & Telemetry Verification Card
worldbuilding.qsl_animation_notes: Seen from the camera bolted to Buoy N-24 itself: in Frame B, a bioluminescent Silt-Strider walks right up to the foreground guy-wire and rubs its neck against the cable, sending cyan capacitive sparks up the wire as the amber Fresnel lamp flashes!

discovery_arc.summary: Logged on 3890 kHz CW/USB; onboard mast-cam confirms a Silt-Strider rubbing directly against Guy-Wire #2, causing -165 Hz pitch bends every 3, 5, and 8 seconds.
Seven Silt-Striders gather during a methane neap tide, detuning the beacon by a full -440 Hz into a minor-seventh chord that triggers GOR-9's Euclidean harmonic detector.
Dr. Moreau confirms the herd has begun vocally mimicking the buoy's 18 WPM Morse ID ('VVV DE TM-N24/B') even when the transmitter steps down!
